title: WAYS TO SELL EXISTING PHYSICAL PRODUCTS
content:
If the physical product already belongs to another company, your next decision is how you want to participate in the sale.

Three common routes are wholesale/reselling, dropshipping, and affiliate/referral marketing. They can all involve the same kind of product while giving you very different responsibilities.

WHOLESALE / RESELLING
You buy inventory and resell it. You may control your storefront, pricing within applicable agreements, presentation, and customer relationship, but you also take on inventory and fulfillment responsibilities.

DROPSHIPPING
You sell the product, but a supplier ships it to the customer. This can reduce inventory handling, while making supplier reliability, shipping, returns, product quality, and customer expectations especially important.

AFFILIATE / REFERRAL
You recommend the product and the merchant handles the transaction and fulfillment. Your compensation and attribution depend on the program's terms.

THE REAL CHOICE
How much of the transaction do you want to own? More control often means more operational responsibility. Less operational responsibility often means more dependence on another business.

A QUICK EXAMPLE
Suppose you want to sell hiking gear. You could buy packs wholesale and ship them yourself, list packs that a supplier ships directly after your customer orders, or recommend packs through a retailer's affiliate program. The product category is the same. Your business role is not.

WHAT CHANGES BETWEEN THESE MODELS

With wholesale/reselling, you usually take possession of inventory before the customer buys. That can give you more control over availability, packaging, bundling, shipping, and the customer experience, but it also puts money into stock that may not sell.

With dropshipping, the supplier holds and ships the inventory. That can lower the amount of stock you personally handle, but the customer may still see YOU as the seller when something arrives late, damaged, incorrect, or not at all. You need to understand exactly who is responsible for what.

With affiliate/referral selling, you usually do not become the seller of record. You send the customer to another merchant, and your income depends on the program correctly attributing the qualifying purchase to you. This can remove fulfillment work while also giving you less control over the transaction.

A DECISION FILTER

Choose WHOLESALE/RESELLING if you are comfortable buying inventory and want more control over the retail transaction.

Choose DROPSHIPPING if you want to operate the storefront or sale but prefer a supplier to hold and ship inventory, and you are comfortable depending heavily on supplier operations.

Choose AFFILIATE/REFERRAL if you would rather recommend products and let another merchant handle checkout, fulfillment, and most customer transaction responsibilities.

None of these labels proves the economics are good. They identify the structure you should investigate next.
